[[File:Luroth quartic.svg|thumb|250px|right|Some examples of '''Lüroth quartics''']]
In mathematics, a '''Lüroth quartic''' is a nonsingular quartic [[plane curve]] containing the 10 vertices of a complete pentalateral. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|first= Jacob |last=Lüroth|authorlink=Jacob Lüroth|year=1869}}. {{harvs|txt|last=Morley|authorlink=Frank Morley|year=1919}} showed that the Lüroth quartics form an open subset of a degree 54 [[hypersurface]], called the '''Lüroth hypersurface''',  in the space '''P'''<sup>14</sup> of all quartics. {{harvtxt|Böhning|von Bothmer|2011}} proved that the moduli space of Lüroth quartics is rational.
